## From Patagonia's glaciers to Rio: how this 12-day private tour works

“Ice, Sun and the End of the World” brings together two countries and very different natural conditions. **The trip is scheduled from February 28 to March 11, 2027**, for **12 days and 11 nights**. Travellers start in [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/), then head south to [El Calafate](/argentina/place/el-calafate/) and [Ushuaia](/argentina/place/ushuaia/). After Patagonia, the climate changes dramatically: [Iguazu](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/) and [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/) complete the journey.

The overall format is private, but some excursions **take place in groups**. This distinction matters more than the word "private" in the title: transfers, accommodation, guides' languages and the format of each excursion should be considered individually.

## Why combine El Calafate and Ushuaia on one trip?

[El Calafate](/argentina/place/el-calafate/) offers Patagonia's glacial landscapes. A whole day is devoted to Perito Moreno Glacier, within Los Glaciares National Park, where an immense ice front reaches Lake Argentino. The focus is on the glacier and mountain scenery, rather than extended city sightseeing.

The second southern stop is [Ushuaia](/argentina/place/ushuaia/), a city on Tierra del Fuego. The programme visits Tierra del Fuego National Park. A trip to Martillo Island, with a walk near penguins, is offered as **a separately paid option**. Penguin encounters must not be treated as a guaranteed part of the standard itinerary.

Patagonia accounts for **4 nights in two cities**: 2 in El Calafate and 2 in Ushuaia. This part suits travellers who want to see southern Argentina's famous sights within limited time and are prepared to fly between remote regions. The schedule is too compact for multi-day hikes with spare days.

## Two days at Iguazu, followed by three nights in Rio

After Ushuaia, the route heads north to [Iguazu Falls](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/). Separate excursions cover the Argentine and Brazilian sides. The Argentine side offers closer access to numerous walkways above the cascades, while the Brazilian side provides a broader view across the waterfall system. These are neighbouring but separate parks on opposite sides of an international border.

Travellers then fly to [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/). Three nights are scheduled there, along with excursions to Sugarloaf Mountain, through the old city and up Corcovado to Christ the Redeemer. After southern Patagonia, Rio feels entirely different: ocean bays and city leisure replace cool mountain landscapes.

The distribution of nights makes the pace clear:

| Stop | Nights |
|---|---:|
| Buenos Aires | 2 |
| El Calafate | 2 |
| Ushuaia | 2 |
| Foz do Iguaçu | 2 |
| Rio de Janeiro | 3 |

## What the price means and how accommodation options differ

The programme offers **3-, 4- and 5-star hotels** and different rates for single, double and triple occupancy. Pricing also depends on the group size. The lowest rate is calculated **per person for 3 travellers sharing a triple room (TRL) in 3-star hotels**. A group of two in DBL accommodation has a different price; the lowest TRL rate cannot be substituted for it.

All arrangements include 2 nights in Ushuaia, but the particular hotel there is confirmed when booking. Hotels at the other stops appear in the main tour page's rate table; a hotel may be replaced by one of the same category.

**Domestic flights are paid for separately:** Buenos Aires — El Calafate — Ushuaia — Foz do Iguaçu — Rio. This substantially affects the total price and the value of the chosen hotel rate. International flights are also excluded from the basic price. Comparing only the starting rate with other journeys would therefore be misleading.

## Languages and format: private guiding or a group?

Private excursions with Russian-speaking guides are provided in Buenos Aires, Foz do Iguaçu and Rio. In El Calafate and Ushuaia, the standard package contains **group excursions in English**. An additional rate for private Russian-language excursions in these two southern cities is available with a minimum of 2 participants.

In Buenos Aires, an included dinner-and-tango show takes place as a group activity without a guide. Pack warm, windproof clothing for Patagonia and lighter waterproof clothing for Iguazu. The contrast between southern Argentina and the tropical border region makes it difficult to travel with just one small set of clothes.

## Who should choose this journey, and who should consider another?

This tour is well suited to travellers whose main interests are **Perito Moreno Glacier, Tierra del Fuego, both sides of Iguazu and several days in Rio**. It connects distant regions but does not include a separate high-altitude crossing through Bolivia and Peru.

To see Uyuni Salt Flat, Lake Titicaca and Machu Picchu as well, compare the [18-day group itinerary through five countries](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-group-tour-18-days/). The logistics and physical demands are quite different. For a more focused exploration, browse [Argentina tours](/argentina/tour/).

## Frequently asked questions about “Ice, Sun and the End of the World”

### Are flights between the cities included?

No. Flights between Buenos Aires, El Calafate, Ushuaia, Foz do Iguaçu and Rio are paid separately, as is the international flight.

### Are all excursions private and in Russian?

No. Private Russian-language sightseeing is included at the three city stops and Iguazu; the standard excursions in El Calafate and Ushuaia are English-speaking group activities. Private Russian-speaking guides in the south are available for a surcharge under the stated conditions.

### Does the itinerary include a penguin visit?

The visit to Martillo Island and a walk near penguins is listed as an additional paid excursion. It is not included in the standard package.

### What does the starting price in the rate table mean?

It is a per-person price for 3 participants in TRL accommodation at 3-star hotels. Two participants, single occupancy or a different hotel category have separate applicable prices.

## Argentina, Patagonia and Iguazu in 12 days: who is this route for?

This **12-day, 11-night** journey combines [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/), [El Calafate](/argentina/place/el-calafate/), [Ushuaia](/argentina/place/ushuaia/) and Iguazu Falls. During a single holiday, you experience city culture, Patagonian ice, Tierra del Fuego's landscapes and subtropical waterfalls.

Although the name emphasises Argentina, the tour includes **the Brazilian side of Iguazu**. Optional excursions to Montevideo can be arranged on request, but Uruguay is not a compulsory country on the main route. The main geographical scope is Argentina and Brazil.

## The order of regions: why start in Buenos Aires?

| Stage | Main experiences |
|---|---|
| Buenos Aires | Historic neighbourhoods, tango and free time |
| El Calafate | Perito Moreno and glacial landscapes |
| Ushuaia | Tierra del Fuego and the southern coastline |
| Iguazu | Waterfalls on both sides of the border |

In [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/), the programme includes tours with a Russian-speaking guide and **a tango show with dinner**. Free hours can be spent exploring the capital independently. Separate excursions to Tigre, a countryside “Fiesta Gaucha” or Montevideo are also available.

The nature-focused parts then begin, with flights between regions. The change from Patagonia to Iguazu is particularly noticeable: temperature, humidity, vegetation and the clothing needed for sightseeing all change.

## El Calafate: Perito Moreno and views of the glacier

The main attraction in the south is [Perito Moreno Glacier](/argentina/place/perito-moreno-glacier/) within Los Glaciares National Park. Equipped walkways and viewing platforms allow visitors to see the ice wall without walking onto the glacier itself.

**Ice trekking** is a separate optional excursion and is not included in the standard programme. It has its own safety procedures, health restrictions and fitness requirements. If your main goal is to step onto the ice, confirm the availability and conditions of that activity before paying.

El Calafate sightseeing is carried out in a group with **an English-speaking guide**. A Russian-speaking guide provided for other parts of the journey does not automatically accompany the group here.

## Ushuaia: the national park and optional penguins

In [Ushuaia](/argentina/place/ushuaia/), [Tierra del Fuego National Park](/argentina/place/tierra-del-fuego-national-park/) is a main attraction, combining forests, lakes, mountain slopes and coastal sections of the Beagle Channel. The park has short paths as well as longer trails; the exact walking route should reflect the weather and participants' abilities.

The programme includes group tours with **English-speaking guides**. A visit to Martillo Island and its penguin colony is described as an optional excursion that can be booked separately. This option includes approximately two hours of navigation and an additional transfer to the port. Its mention does not mean it is included on every departure.

Even during the warmer season, Tierra del Fuego can have strong winds, rain and cold. Waterproof clothing, warm layers and closed shoes are useful.

## Iguazu: two sides and different waterfall excursions

The final nature section visits Iguazu Falls on the Argentine and [Brazilian sides](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/). In Argentina, established paths lead past individual cascades and the Devil's Throat; the Brazilian side offers broad views of the whole waterfall system.

The “Great Adventure”, Bird Park and a helicopter flight over the falls are **optional extras**, not part of the basic package. The original conditions specify approximately 1 hour 15 minutes for the “Great Adventure” and an age restriction: **not suitable for children under 12**. A Macuco Safari boat excursion on the Brazilian side is mentioned as an alternative.

The excursion involves crossing an international border. Necessary documents and the right to re-enter must be checked for the traveller's nationality.

## What is included and what is paid separately?

The basic price of our journey is **from $4,216**. It includes **4-star hotels** with breakfast, private driver transfers, entrance tickets on the main itinerary, private excursions with Russian-speaking guides in Buenos Aires and Iguazu, group excursions with English-speaking guides in El Calafate and Ushuaia, and a tango show with dinner.

**International and domestic flights are not included.** Optional excursions, tips, early check-in, late checkout and personal expenses are also paid separately.

An important feature is the mixed service format. Private transfers do not mean that every excursion is private and conducted in Russian. The Patagonian tours are group excursions in English.

## Who should choose this option?

This journey suits travellers who want to combine Argentina and Brazil in one trip, balancing city sightseeing with natural wonders. Compared with the [13-day journey covering the same key regions](/multi-country/tour/incredible-argentina-patagonia/), **domestic flights are paid for separately** on this tour, which matters when comparing the total cost.

For a shorter holiday with a glacier and Iguazu but without Ushuaia, consider the [10-day itinerary](/multi-country/tour/argentina-glaciers-to-iguazu-falls/).

## Frequently asked questions about the 12-day Argentina–Iguazu tour

### Are domestic flights included?

No. International and domestic air tickets are listed as additional expenses.

### Is there a Russian-speaking guide everywhere?

No. Russian-language guiding is provided on private excursions in Buenos Aires and Iguazu. In El Calafate and Ushuaia, group tours use English-speaking guides.

### Is the Montevideo excursion included?

It is offered separately on request. Montevideo is not a required stage of this tour.

### Can I book glacier trekking?

Yes. It is offered as a separately paid option with its own participation and safety conditions.

## Argentina, Chile and Bolivia in 18 days: highlands, cruise and Patagonia

**This 18-day Ada Tours itinerary covers 3 countries and combines very different travel styles.** First come [Santiago de Chile](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/), desert plateaus and Uyuni Salt Flat, followed by [Torres del Paine](/chile/place/puerto-natales-torres-del-paine/), an expedition cruise from Punta Arenas to Ushuaia, Buenos Aires and the lake district around Bariloche.

It is best regarded as **an extensive combined journey with a distinct sea voyage**, rather than an ordinary tour of capital cities. Transport, altitude and weather change frequently, and the cruise includes shore excursions with different levels of difficulty.

## The itinerary sequence and distribution of days

| Days | Main region |
|---|---|
| 1–4 | Santiago, Atacama, Uyuni |
| 5–11 | Torres del Paine, cruise, Ushuaia |
| 12–18 | Buenos Aires, Bariloche |

The trip opens with an introduction to Santiago. Travellers then head towards San Pedro de Atacama and cross Bolivia's high-altitude regions by off-road vehicle. The next major destination is [Uyuni Salt Flat](/bolivia/place/uyuni/), with nearby lagoons and volcanoes.

Back in Chile, the Patagonian section begins: [Puerto Natales and Torres del Paine](/chile/place/puerto-natales-torres-del-paine/), followed by [Punta Arenas](/chile/place/punta-arenas/) and embarkation. The sea route includes Ainsworth Bay, the Tucker Islets, Pia Glacier, the Beagle Channel and Cape Horn. After arriving in [Ushuaia](/argentina/place/ushuaia/), you visit Tierra del Fuego National Park.

The last part takes place in Argentina. In [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/), the programme includes city sightseeing, New Year's Eve dinner and tango. Then comes a flight to [Bariloche](/argentina/place/bariloche/), road trips along lakes and a catamaran excursion to Victoria Island and the Arrayanes Forest.

## The high-altitude section: why preparation matters

During the first days, you move rapidly from city elevations to Bolivia's desert plateaus and lagoons. The journey includes Laguna Colorada, other colourful lakes, geothermal fields and volcanoes. Overnight stays are at altitude, where even a short walk can feel different from one at sea level.

[Uyuni](/bolivia/place/uyuni/) sits at approximately 3,650 metres. Travelling on the Altiplano calls for warm clothes and sun protection, and it is best to consider your tolerance for altitude before departure. Physical demands cannot be judged by distance alone: the altitude itself and the length of travel on rough roads also matter.

The appearance of the salt flat changes with the season. A white salt surface and reflections of the sky after rain are different states of the same landscape. A layer of water can restrict driving along the usual route.

## What happens on the fjord cruise?

The sea section follows the overland excursion in Torres del Paine. Travellers transfer to Punta Arenas and embark on a ship heading south through the Strait of Magellan, the fjords of Tierra del Fuego and the Beagle Channel.

**Shore landings use small Zodiac boats.** At Ainsworth Bay, there are walking routes of different difficulty, including an easier walk and a moraine trail. At [Pia Glacier](/chile/place/pia-glacier/), travellers can also choose between a scenic walk and a more challenging ascent.

[Cape Horn](/chile/place/cape-horn/) is included in the sailing itinerary, but **landing ashore depends on wind and sea conditions**. Even on a scheduled cruise, the captain may change the order of activities if conditions are unsafe. During the penguin season, the Tucker Islets are particularly interesting for birdlife; at other times, the programme may substitute Brookes Bay.

If you mainly want the ship journey without Bolivia and Bariloche, compare it with the standalone [5-day “Tierra del Fuego Fjords” cruise](/multi-country/tour/tierra-del-fuego-fjords/). The longer tour combines this voyage with overland travel and flights.

## New Year and the city programme

The current itinerary is organised around **December 20 to January 6** and includes a New Year's celebration in Buenos Aires. Maintaining the precise sequence of days is particularly important here: changing the festive evening or sea voyage affects all subsequent logistics and accommodation.

After the holiday come city excursions and then Bariloche. The landscape changes again in the lake region: wooded slopes, high mountains and Lake Nahuel Huapi replace desert and windswept fjords. You explore the surrounding area by road and take catamaran excursions. This is a substantial third part of the journey, not a brief technical stop before departure.

## Who is this tour for, and what should you consider?

The itinerary suits travellers who want to combine **a cruise, natural landmarks in three countries, New Year and city experiences**. Eighteen days involve several flights and transfers, with few extended periods of rest at a single hotel. Some stages use off-road vehicles, others a ship or walking trails.

Consider your tolerance for seasickness, whether the selected walks suit you and how comfortable you are at Altiplano elevations. Hotels and the cruise cabin category are tied to the particular date sequence in the current tour description.

## How does the 12-day alternative differ?

The shorter [“Patagonia and Uyuni Salt Flat in 12 Days” itinerary](/multi-country/tour/patagonia-uyuni-salt-flats-12-days/) retains experiences in Argentina, Chilean Patagonia and Bolivia, but **does not include the separate multi-day sea cruise ending in Ushuaia** or the extended Bariloche section. It suits travellers with less time.

When choosing, compare not only the number of countries but also the travel style: glacier and park sightseeing is different from cruise landings and mountain expeditions.

## Frequently asked questions about the 18-day journey

### Is the cruise a main or optional part of the itinerary?

The fjord cruise is included in the sequence of the full 18-day journey. It is a distinct sea section within the three-country tour.

### Is landing at Cape Horn guaranteed?

No. The captain decides according to weather, waves and safety. If landing is impossible, the ship's programme is adjusted.

### Does the tour include Bariloche?

Yes. Bariloche and its lake district occupy several days in the final section, including road and water excursions.

### Where is New Year celebrated?

Under the current programme, New Year's Eve is spent in Buenos Aires after the cruise and the visit to Ushuaia.

## Argentina and Chile: a 13-day journey through Patagonia

This [13-day tour of Argentina and Chile](/multi-country/tour/argentina-chile-patagonia-13-days/) covers several contrasting Patagonian regions. From Buenos Aires, the route heads to [Ushuaia](/argentina/place/ushuaia/) on Tierra del Fuego, then [Perito Moreno Glacier](/argentina/place/perito-moreno-glacier/), the walking trails around [El Chaltén](/argentina/place/el-chalten/) and Chile's [Torres del Paine](/chile/place/puerto-natales-torres-del-paine/). The journey ends in Santiago de Chile with a visit to the Maipo wine region.

The trip lasts **13 days and 12 nights**. The distinctive feature of this private itinerary is the dedicated hiking days around El Chaltén. It appeals to travellers who want more than views from a vehicle and observation platforms, and would like to walk Patagonia's mountain trails.

## Geography and itinerary stages

| Days | Travel region |
| --- | --- |
| 1–2 | Buenos Aires |
| 3–5 | Ushuaia and Tierra del Fuego |
| 6 | El Calafate and Perito Moreno |
| 7–8 | El Chaltén and mountain trails |
| 9–10 | Chile: Puerto Natales and Torres del Paine |
| 11–13 | Santiago, Maipo and departure |

Unlike a short nature-park tour, this journey devotes more time to varied environments: ocean channels, subantarctic forests, glaciers, rocky mountain terrain and granite towers.

## Buenos Aires: starting with neighbourhoods and tango

The first two days take place in [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/). On arrival, there is a transfer and free time; day two includes a private city sightseeing tour with a Russian-speaking guide. The itinerary names La Boca, San Telmo, Plaza de Mayo, Casa Rosada, the Obelisk, Recoleta and modern neighbourhoods.

An evening tango show with dinner is included. This day brings a cultural element before the journey heads far south, where weather and roads between parks play a major role.

## Ushuaia: lakes, forests and Tierra del Fuego National Park

On day three, travellers fly to [Ushuaia](/argentina/place/ushuaia/), a city near the southern tip of South America on the Beagle Channel. Day four focuses on Tierra del Fuego's natural attractions, including lakes Fagnano and Escondido.

On day five, you visit [Tierra del Fuego National Park](/argentina/place/tierra-del-fuego-national-park/), known for its coastal landscapes, forests and mountain slopes. The route then continues to [El Calafate](/argentina/place/el-calafate/).

This distinguishes the 13-day option: Ushuaia is not included on the 10-day VIP Argentina-and-Chile programme.

## Perito Moreno: an ice front on Lake Argentino

On day six, the tour visits [Perito Moreno](/argentina/place/perito-moreno-glacier/) in [Los Glaciares National Park](/argentina/place/los-glaciares-national-park/). From the viewing walkways, visitors watch the ice wall and deep crevasses. The glacier front moves and changes, offering a close view of a dynamic natural process; a particular ice calving event cannot be guaranteed.

This is one of the key nature days in both Patagonia options: the shorter VIP journey and the longer 13-day tour.

## El Chaltén: Laguna Capri and Laguna de los Tres

Day seven includes a transfer to [El Chaltén](/argentina/place/el-chalten/) and a hike towards [Laguna Capri](/argentina/place/laguna-capri/). This mountain lake offers views of granite peaks when the weather permits. The outing introduces the area gradually before a more demanding trail.

Day eight is devoted to hiking to [Laguna de los Tres](/argentina/place/laguna-de-los-tres/) beneath the Fitz Roy massif. Good fitness, suitable footwear and attention to the weather are essential. The final sections can be steep and rocky. Trail accessibility and actual walking demands depend on conditions, so they should be confirmed when choosing travel dates.

This is the main difference from a sightseeing-only Patagonia trip: **two consecutive days are devoted to mountain trails near El Chaltén**.

## Crossing into Chile and visiting Torres del Paine

On day nine, participants travel to Chile's [Puerto Natales](/chile/place/puerto-natales-torres-del-paine/). Day ten focuses on Torres del Paine National Park. Its lakes, glacial valleys and granite towers show another side of Patagonia compared with Argentina's Los Glaciares.

Distinguish park sightseeing from the multi-day W and O trekking circuits. The 13-day tour includes Torres del Paine but does not list a separate multi-day W or O trek.

On day eleven, the approved programme calls for a transfer or flight to Santiago de Chile.

## Santiago de Chile and the Maipo wine valley

The final days are spent in [Santiago](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/). The itinerary includes city sightseeing with a Russian-speaking guide and a visit to the [Maipo Valley](/chile/place/maipo-valley/), home to vineyards and wineries. Day thirteen is the end of the tour and departure.

After glaciers, trails and border crossings, this is a calmer city section. It offers another view of Chile through its capital and wine traditions.

## Guides, flights and price

Included are hotel stays, transfers and excursions as specified, and meals on the designated days. **Russian-speaking guides** are scheduled for Buenos Aires and Santiago, with **English-speaking guides** at the other excursion stops.

The tour price is **from $8,416**. International flights are not included. **Domestic flights cost an additional amount from $900 per person**, while optional excursions, meals and drinks not specified in the programme, tips and laundry are also extra. At a minimum, these domestic air tickets need to be considered on top of the base rate when planning the actual budget.

## Who is this journey for?

The 13-day itinerary suits travellers especially interested in **Tierra del Fuego and hiking near Fitz Roy**. If you prefer comfortable sightseeing around Perito Moreno, Torres del Paine and the Strait of Magellan, compare the [10-day VIP Patagonia tour](/multi-country/tour/luxury-patagonia-10-days/).

For Argentine glaciers together with waterfalls and beaches, consider the [11-day Argentina–Brazil itinerary](/multi-country/tour/argentina-brazil-buenos-aires-el-calafate-iguazu-pipa-11-days/). Other geographical combinations are available in the [multi-country tour catalogue](/multi-country/).

## Frequently asked questions about the 13-day Patagonia tour

### Are hiking excursions included?

Yes. Days 7 and 8 include Laguna Capri and Laguna de los Tres near El Chaltén.

### Is Tierra del Fuego on the itinerary?

Yes. It includes Ushuaia, lakes Fagnano and Escondido and Tierra del Fuego National Park.

### Do all guides speak Russian?

No. Russian-speaking guides lead the Buenos Aires and Santiago excursions; other sections have English-speaking guides.

### Are domestic flights paid separately?

Yes. The tour terms specify additional domestic flight expenses **from $900 per person**.

## From Perito Moreno Glacier to Iguazu Falls: Argentina and Brazil in 10 days

This **10-day, 9-night** itinerary brings together three experiences: [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/) with its architecture and tango, [El Calafate](/argentina/place/el-calafate/) with [Perito Moreno Glacier](/argentina/place/perito-moreno-glacier/), and Iguazu's cascades on both the Argentine and Brazilian sides.

For travellers with limited time, the itinerary combines southern and northeastern Argentina in a single holiday. Unlike longer Patagonia programmes, there is no mandatory stop at Ushuaia. Time is concentrated on the three main regions, although flights between them are still necessary.

## The three main parts of the journey

| Where | Why go |
|---|---|
| Buenos Aires | Architecture, neighbourhoods and a tango show |
| El Calafate | Perito Moreno and Patagonian scenery |
| Iguazu | Waterfalls on both sides of the border |

In the capital, tours with Russian-speaking guides feature historic neighbourhoods, major squares and a tango show with dinner. Free time can be spent walking independently or choosing an additional outing beyond the city.

**Uruguay** is listed among possible optional destinations through Montevideo but is not a principal mandatory country of this trip. Brazil, by contrast, belongs to the main itinerary through the visit to the Brazilian side of Iguazu.

## Perito Moreno: a glacier excursion without mandatory ice walking

The [Perito Moreno Glacier](/argentina/place/perito-moreno-glacier/) area has established platforms and walking paths offering views of the glacier from a safe distance. The characteristic sounds and movement of ice can be observed from viewing points, but large icefalls occur unpredictably.

**Ice trekking on the glacier costs an additional $360 per person** under the programme terms. It is not part of the basic excursion and requires special organisation, equipment and compliance with the operator's restrictions.

In El Calafate, the excursion is conducted **as a group with an English-speaking guide**. Travellers preferring Russian-language information throughout the trip should therefore anticipate a change of language on this Patagonian section.

The national park administration recommends checking trail conditions in advance, wearing waterproof clothing and comfortable footwear, and staying within designated areas when viewing the glacier.

## Iguazu: two perspectives on one waterfall system

Travelling from Patagonia to Iguazu brings a dramatic change of conditions: humid subtropical air replaces cold winds and glacial landscapes. On the Argentine side, walkways run beside individual falls; the [Brazilian side](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/) offers a wide panorama of the entire system.

Visiting both sides requires crossing an international border. Travellers should check documents for Argentina and Brazil, re-entry requirements and border-crossing times based on nationality.

The programme includes excursions with **a Russian-speaking guide at Iguazu**. Optional water activities should not be assumed part of the basic package unless separately confirmed.

## Optional trips from Buenos Aires

The programme lists several choices for a free day. These are alternatives, not mandatory visits:

- **Tigre and the northern suburbs** — $100 per person.
- **“Fiesta Gaucha”** — $250 per person.
- **Montevideo** — a shared excursion with an English-speaking guide at $400 per person, or a private excursion with a Russian-speaking guide for a minimum of 2 people at $650 per person.

It is not planned to take all these excursions on the same free day. Choose according to your priorities: delta scenery, rural traditions or visiting another country. Montevideo also requires consideration of the crossing and border documentation.

## Price and service terms

The basic price of our journey is **from $2,563**. Included are **4-star hotel accommodation** with breakfast, private driver transfers, excursions with Russian-speaking guides in Buenos Aires and Iguazu, a group excursion with an English-speaking guide in El Calafate, entrance tickets and a tango show with dinner.

**International and domestic flights are paid for separately.** Optional excursions, tips, early check-in, late checkout and personal expenses are also excluded. The budget needs to account for the flights between three regions rather than relying only on the land package price.

## Choosing between 10, 12 and 13 days

The 10-day option suits travellers who want three contrasting regions without a separate Tierra del Fuego stage. The [12-day programme including Ushuaia](/multi-country/tour/argentina-buenos-aires-el-calafate-ushuaia-iguazu-12-days/) adds the southern national park and coast. The [13-day itinerary](/multi-country/tour/incredible-argentina-patagonia/) includes Ushuaia and domestic flights within the package.

Compare not only duration, but the languages of guides, included flights, ice activities and the amount of free time.

## Frequently asked questions about “From Glaciers to Waterfalls”

### Is ice trekking included?

No. Glacier trekking is an optional excursion; the programme gives a separate cost of $360 per person.

### Will there be a Russian-speaking guide in El Calafate?

The basic El Calafate excursion is a group tour with an English-speaking guide. Russian-speaking guides are specified for Buenos Aires and Iguazu.

### Is Montevideo available?

Yes, as an optional excursion from Buenos Aires. It is an additional journey to Uruguay, not a mandatory part of the 10-day itinerary.

### Are flights between regions included?

No. Domestic and international air tickets are paid separately.
